- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is high, reduce forecast slightly to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.3) and forecast is low, raise forecast modestly to avoid underreaction.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a recent low, cap the overshoot by limiting the next 3–5 days’ forecast increase.  
- If forecast consistently lags true outcome by 1–2 days, adjust forward-looking models to anticipate 1–2-day lag in price behavior.  
- In periods of high volatility (sentiment swings > 0.5), apply mean reversion bias: if forecast deviates > 5% from recent 7-day average, pull back toward that average.  
- For 30-day horizon, avoid extreme outliers (±10% from 14-day moving average) unless sentiment strongly supports them.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and forecast is consistently off, use sentiment as a smoothing factor — reduce forecast variance by 20% in such cases.
